content.comment_body: I am using four [product_name] controllers in a server-client network, but the clocks on each device gradually drift apart. After about a week, the difference can reach several minutes. Is there a way for the [product_name] devices to synchronize their clocks with each other?
From what I understand, you will need a time server for your network setup. Clock synchronization between [product_name] controllers is not possible without a time server.
Understood. Where do I configure the time server for the [product_name] devices? Is it possible to use an NTP server from the internet, like time.windows.com, as the time source?

analysis.insight_summary: Users are facing challenges with keeping clocks synchronized across multiple [product_name] controllers in a network, resulting in time drift over the span of a week. The main takeaway is that these devices cannot automatically align their clocks without an external time server, which complicates keeping accurate time across several units.
analysis.user_expectations: Users hope for built-in time synchronization among [product_name] controllers or straightforward configuration allowing them to connect to NTP servers for automatic time alignment.
